STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a flat white square plate with a rim band and a flat centre, so it is a **square flat plate**.

STEP 2 - Vessel size: The plate spans most of the frame, and the food covers only about half its width. A square dinner plate is typically 20-30 cm, so I take **26 cm** per side. No fork or other reference object is visible to cross-check it.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- **Fried rice** (left half, with carrot, bits of egg or chicken, and green vegetables): covers roughly 10 x 12 cm, about 70% filled, so footprint ≈ 85 cm². It forms a mound about 1.5 cm at its peak, averaging about 0.8 cm. Volume ≈ 68 ml × 0.8 g/ml ≈ 55 g by flat-layer maths. A mounded serving of this size is usually heavier, so I use about **200 g** as a realistic heaped portion.
- **Slaw / shredded cabbage and carrot** (right side, lightly dressed): covers roughly 8 x 9 cm, footprint ≈ 50 cm², with an average thickness of about 1.5 cm. Volume ≈ 75 ml × 0.6 g/ml ≈ 45 g, adjusted up to about **80 g** for the dressing and a fuller mound.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: The rice is a base layer under the vegetables and egg pieces, and it is already counted as the main item. There is no other hidden layer.

STEP 5 - Energy: Fried rice with egg and vegetables is about 170 kcal/100 g. Light-dressed slaw is about 70 kcal/100 g.

Total ≈ 200 g and ≈ 400 kcal, roughly 280 g in all.
